title: Arizona Innovation Map
subtitle: Learning about Arizona’s semiconductor industry through a map.
html:
Open Arizona Innovation Map ↗

Project overview

I built Arizona Innovation Map to understand what materials, equipment, and services a fab needs nearby, and where those companies and institutions are located. I organized public information into an interactive map so I could connect each location with its role.

What I learned

I grouped locations into the semiconductor supply chain, businesses, and institutions and added search, a list, site details, and public sources. The project helped me learn how manufacturing, packaging, materials, equipment, facilities, and logistics fit together.

Learning from the manufacturing process

I started with the stages in Arizona Chip Journey and used the map to find Arizona companies that provide relevant materials, equipment, or services. Campuses, government offices, and selected businesses helped me place that industry knowledge in context.

How to use the map

Choose a category, then open a location from the map or list to read its description and sources. Arizona Chip Journey explains where materials and equipment fit in the process. Ecosystem Network shows the roles of different organizations and infrastructure.

Local Phoenix 3D prototype

In a local prototype, I brought company search, site details, and a 3D map of Phoenix onto one page to explore how a spatial view can help present industry information.

Reading the data

This map documents my personal learning. Locations are based on public information, and approximate locations are labeled. Supplier or partnership relationships require separate public evidence.
